correctness.rationale: The exact regression follows from conditional exchangeability of distinct partners of the first exposed vertices and three disjoint crossing categories, with probabilities 1/2, 1/3 and 1/3. Subtracting survival-weighted means gives the displayed quadratic, including the terminal boundary. A strict increasing-regression covariance argument proves the finite sign. Survival-tail domination and Rayleigh moments yield the leading covariance, and the classical crossing variance yields the correlation scaling. Exhaustive independent rational enumeration of 146598 matchings for n=2..7 matches every conditional mean and survival value; enumeration is not used to prove all-size claims.

value.rationale: The first completion time controls when the first pair becomes observable in the memory-pairing model, whereas crossings measure global chord interlacing. Their positive, strictly increasing exact conditional regression and divergent covariance despite vanishing correlation identify a nontrivial cross-scale dependence mechanism. This is not a mere marginal-moment restatement or normalization and gives exact finite predictive means together with an asymptotic joint scaling constant.
